who: William M. Fowler Jr., historian of American and maritime history at Northeastern University, PhD Notre Dame 1971.

evidence.says: William M. Fowler Jr. earned his doctorate at Notre Dame in 1971, joined Northeastern that year, and resumed teaching there after directing the Massachusetts Historical Society through 2005. His fields include maritime and New England history.
The authority identifies William Worthington Fowler, author of Woman of the American frontier (1877).
The item identifies William Warde Fowler, an ornithologist and classical scholar employed at Oxford.
The Will Fowler authority identifies the University of St Andrews professor of Latin American studies and author of Santa Anna of Mexico.

notes: None of the three candidates is Northeastern's William M. Fowler Jr.; their full names, institutions and works identify different people.

who: R. Blakeslee Gilpin, historian of slavery and its legacies at Tulane University, PhD Yale 2009.

evidence.says: Tulane lists R. Blakeslee Gilpin as an associate professor of history, with a Yale PhD awarded in 2009, and identifies John Brown Still Lives! as his first book.
The candidate authority identifies Robert George Gilpin Jr., an international relations scholar and Princeton professor, author of American scientists and nuclear weapons (1962).

notes: The Tulane historian and the Princeton international relations scholar are different people.

who: Hines H. Hall, historian at Auburn University, PhD Vanderbilt.

evidence.says: Auburn lists Hines H. Hall as associate professor emeritus of history, with a Vanderbilt PhD, Auburn MA and Duke BA; the emeritus entry is dated July 2006.
The candidate authority expands H. Duncan Hall to Hessel Duncan Hall and identifies an international-law specialist, historian and public servant associated with North American supply.

notes: Hines H. Hall and Hessel Duncan Hall are distinct full-name identities.

who: Joseph Righton Robertson Jr., medieval historian, University of Maryland; doctorate Emory.

evidence.says: Maryland faculty 1962–1973; master's and doctorate in medieval history from Emory.
The candidate authority identifies Joseph Robertson, author of Scotch parliamentary elections in the seventeenth century (1859).

notes: The candidate is the nineteenth-century author, a different person from the Maryland supervisor.

who: John Corwin Rule, historian of early modern France at Ohio State University, PhD Harvard 1958.

evidence.says: The AHA identifies John Corwin Rule as Ohio State professor emeritus, with a Harvard PhD completed in 1958 on the Treaty of Utrecht negotiations; he joined Ohio State in 1958.

The candidate authority expands the name to John Graham Rule, with a Warwick PhD and a Southampton history lectureship from 1968; it links him to The experience of labour in eighteenth century industry.

notes: John Corwin Rule at Ohio State and John Graham Rule at Southampton have different doctorates, institutions and fields.

who: L. Christian Smith, historian of American popular culture at Arizona State University, PhD Illinois 1972.

evidence.says: ASU identifies Professor Emeritus L. Christian Smith as an American popular-culture historian who received his Illinois PhD in 1972 and taught at ASU from 1971 to 2010.
The candidate authority identifies Laurajane Smith, a heritage-studies and archaeology scholar associated with York and the Australian National University.
ANU identifies Laurajane Smith as professor of Heritage and Museum Studies with a University of Sydney PhD in heritage studies/archaeology awarded in 1996.

notes: Laurajane Smith is a different scholar; the supervisor's institution, doctorate and field all differ.

who: Lorenzo M. Crowell, historian at Mississippi State University.

evidence.says: Mississippi State's archived catalogue identifies Lorenzo M. Crowell as associate professor emeritus of history.
The candidate authority expands L. A. Crowell Sr. to Lester Avant Crowell Sr., a physician in Lincolnton and author of Old age deferred.

notes: The physician Lester Avant Crowell Sr. is a different person from the historian Lorenzo M. Crowell.

who: Jeffrey Burds, historian of Russia and the Soviet Union at Northeastern University, PhD Yale 1990.

evidence.says: Northeastern identifies Jeffrey Burds as an associate professor of history educated at Yale, specializing in Soviet history and author of Holocaust in Rovno and Soviet Informants' Networks.
Yale's history dissertation list records Jeffrey Burds in 1990 with Patterns of Change in the Central Russian Village: Community Relations and the Market Economy, 1840–1914.
The authority identifies Jeffrey Burds, links to Wikidata Q59610241, and associates him with Peasant Dreams & Market Politics.
The publisher's author biography for Peasant Dreams and Market Politics identifies Jeffrey Burds as associate professor of Russian and Soviet history at Northeastern University.

notes: The authority's publication identity, Northeastern affiliation and Yale 1990 doctorate agree; the automatic age flag does not establish a different person.
